title: Control plane: add Dedicated scaling policy schema (min/max bounds + predictive toggle)
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Summary
Adds control plane schema + persistence scaffolding for per-deployment autoscaling policy on Redwood Dedicated. This PR introduces customer-configurable min/max capacity bounds and a predictive autoscaling mode toggle at the schema layer only (no autoscaler behavior changes in this PR).

Motivation
Enterprise Dedicated customers are asking for explicit guardrails around scaling: (1) a hard ceiling to control spend, (2) a hard floor to preserve baseline throughput/SLOs, and (3) an opt-in predictive mode to reduce queue buildup during known ramps. We need these fields in the control plane first so Console/API work and autoscaler enforcement can follow behind feature flags.

What changed
- Introduced a new ScalingPolicyV1 object on Dedicated deployments:
  - min_replicas (optional)
  - max_replicas (optional)
  - scale_up_cooldown_seconds (optional)
  - scale_down_cooldown_seconds (optional)
  - predictive_mode (enum: OFF | ADVISORY | ACTIVE)
  - reactive_fallback (bool; default true when predictive_mode != OFF)
- Validation rules:
  - min_replicas >= 0
  - max_replicas >= 0
  - if both set: min_replicas <= max_replicas
  - cooldown seconds must be within [0, 3600] (0 means "no additional cooldown beyond platform defaults")
  - predictive_mode cannot be ACTIVE unless deployment is Dedicated (guard to prevent accidental use in Hosted)
- Defaulting/backward compatibility:
  - Fields are nullable and do not alter existing behavior unless autoscaler + API enablement is turned on (follow-up PRs).
  - If scaling_policy is absent, evaluation continues to use platform defaults.
- Migration scaffolding:
  - Adds the new column / JSON blob storage slot for scaling_policy on the dedicated_deployments row (implementation detail: JSONB payload with versioned schema).
  - Includes no-op backfill migration to initialize the field to NULL (explicitly not setting defaults to avoid unintended behavior changes).
- Telemetry hooks (schema-level only):
  - Adds structured validation error codes returned by the control plane so Console can render field-specific error states later.

Out of scope
- Autoscaler enforcement (clamping desired replicas to min/max) (tracked in ENG-22140)
- Predictive signal ingestion + forecast interface (tracked in ENG-22142)
- Console endpoints + RBAC wiring for update operations (tracked in ENG-22144 / PR-48252)

Testing
- Unit tests for schema validation and error mapping
- Migration tests: apply/rollback on a representative dedicated_deployments fixture

Rollout notes
- This PR is safe to land on its own: the fields are stored but unused until feature flags are enabled and autoscaler support is deployed.
- Follow-up PRs will add: policy evaluation service behavior, autoscaler clamp + metrics, and Console UI.

References
- Linear: ENG-22141, PM-1842
- ADR draft referenced in architecture thread: autoscaling bounds precedence + safety invariants (pending merge)

Checklist
- [x] Schema versioned and backwards compatible
- [x] Validation errors return stable, documented error codes
- [x] Migration is additive and safe to roll back
- [x] Tests cover edge cases (min > max, negative values, cooldown bounds)

review_conversation: Ethan Park (review): Please make predictive_mode an enum rather than a boolean. We’re likely to need an intermediate state for "advisory" / shadow eval.
Benji Okafor (author): Agreed. Updated to OFF | ADVISORY | ACTIVE. Validation now blocks ACTIVE outside Dedicated.
Jordan Lee (review): Validation should return stable error codes for Console; please avoid string matching on message bodies.
Benji Okafor (author): Added ScalingPolicyValidationErrorCode and mapped to API errors with field paths.
Michael Nguyen (review): Migration should be additive and avoid backfilling defaults; otherwise we risk changing behavior when autoscaler starts reading it.
Benji Okafor (author): Migration now adds JSONB column only; no backfill beyond NULL. Left a follow-up note for ENG-22153 to handle defaults under a flag.
Chloe Martin (review): Can we ensure cooldown bounds are not "magic"? Add constants and tests for min/max allowed values.
Benji Okafor (author): Added COOLDOWN_SECONDS_MIN/MAX constants and expanded test coverage.
Ethan Park (approval): Looks good. Please link the ADR once merged; otherwise fine to proceed.
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved after enum + error code changes.
release_notes: Internal: Adds control plane schema fields for Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) and predictive mode toggle. No behavior change until autoscaler and API enablement land behind feature flags.
